questions.q: The wavenumber of first spectral line of Lyman series of $\mathrm{He}^{+}$ion is $x \mathrm{~m}^{-1}$. What is the wavenumber (in $\mathrm{m}^{-1}$ ) of second spectral line of Balmer series of $\mathrm{Li}^{2+}$ ion?

For Lyman $\begin{aligned} & \overline{\mathrm{v}}=\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}} \times \mathrm{Z}^2\left[\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_1^2}-\frac{1}{\mathrm{n}_2^2}\right] \\ & =\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}} \times 2^2\left[\frac{1}{1^2}-\frac{1}{2^2}\right] \\ & =\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}} \times 4 \times \frac{3}{4} \\ & \overline{\mathrm{v}}=3 \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}=\mathrm{x} \\ & \mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}}=\frac{\mathrm{x}}{3}...(i) \end{aligned}$
For Balmer series $\begin{aligned} & \overline{\mathrm{v}}=\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}} \times 3^2 \times\left[\frac{1}{2^2}-\frac{1}{4^2}\right] \\ & =\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{H}} 9 \times \frac{3}{16}. \end{aligned}$
Putting the value of $R_H$ from eq. (i) $\bar{v}=\frac{x}{3} \times 9 \times \frac{3}{16}=\frac{9 x}{16}$

Given that $5 A^{-1}=\left[\begin{array}{ccc}-3 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & -3\end{array}\right]$
Post multiply by $A$ on both sides $\begin{aligned} & 5 I=\left[\begin{array}{ccc} -3 & 2 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & 2 \\ 2 & 2 & -3 \end{array}\right]\left[\begin{array}{lll} x & y & y \\ y & x & y \\ y & y & x \end{array}\right] \\ & \Rightarrow\left[\begin{array}{ccc} 5 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 5 \end{array}\right]=\left[\begin{array}{ccc} -3 x+4 y & 2 x-y & 2 x-y \\ 2 x-y & -3 x+4 y & 2 x-y \\ 2 x-y & 2 x-y & -3 x+4 y \end{array}\right] \\ & \therefore-3 x+4 y=5...(i) \\ & 2 x-y=0....(ii) \end{aligned}$

Post multiply by $A$, we get $5 I=A^2-4 A$.

questions.solution:
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \boldsymbol{X}=\boldsymbol{x} & 2 & 3 & 5 & 9 \\\hline \boldsymbol{P}(\boldsymbol{X}=\boldsymbol{x}) & K & 2 K & 3 K^2 & K^2 \\\hline\end{array} \\ We know $\Sigma P=1,4 K^2+2 K+K=1K=\frac{1}{4}$ or $(-1$ rejected) ($P$ is always $+ve$)
$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline \boldsymbol{X}=\boldsymbol{x} & 2 & 3 & 5 & 9 \\\hline \boldsymbol{P}(\boldsymbol{X}=\boldsymbol{x}) & \frac{1}{4} & \frac{1}{2} & \frac{3}{16} & \frac{1}{16} \\\hline\end{array}
$\begin{aligned}
& \text {Variance }=E\left(X^2\right)-[E(X)]^2 \\
& E(X)=x \times P=2 \times \frac{1}{4}+3 \times \frac{1}{2}+5 \times \frac{3}{16}+\frac{9}{16}=\frac{7}{2} \\
& E\left(X^2\right)=x^2 \times P=4 \times \frac{1}{4}+9 \times \frac{1}{2}+25 \times \frac{3}{16}+\frac{81}{16}=\frac{61}{4} \\
& \text {Variance }=\frac{64}{4}-\left(\frac{7}{2}\right)^2=\frac{61}{4}-\frac{49}{4}=\frac{12}{4}=3 \\
& \therefore \text { Variance }=3 .
\end{aligned}$

If $p_1$ and $p_2$ are the perpendicular distances from the origin to the planes $\pi_1$ and $\pi_2$ respectively, then $p_1-p_2=$
questions.solution:
Vector equation of plane $p$ passing through $\vec{a}$ and normal vector $\vec{n}$ is given by $(\vec{r}-\vec{a}) \cdot \vec{n}=0$ So, vector equation of plane $\pi_1=\vec{r} \cdot \vec{n}_1=\vec{a}_1 \cdot \vec{n}_1\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \vec{r} \cdot(\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k})=(3 \hat{i}-7 \hat{j}+5 \hat{k}) \cdot(\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k}) \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{r} \cdot(\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k})=-21 \end{aligned}$
Normal form of plane $\pi_1=\vec{r} \cdot\left(\frac{\hat{i}+2 \hat{j}-2 \hat{k}}{3}\right)=\left|\frac{-21}{3}\right| \quad\left(\vec{r} \cdot \hat{n}_1=1\right)$ (Dividing both sides by 3 ) Distance of $\pi_1$ from origin, $p_1=7$ unit Similarly, vector equation of plane $\begin{aligned} & \pi_2=\vec{r} \cdot \vec{n}_2=\vec{a}_2 \cdot \vec{n}_2 \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{r} \cdot(3 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+6 \hat{k})=(2 \hat{i}+7 \hat{j}-8 \hat{k}) \cdot(3 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+6 \hat{k}) \\ & \Rightarrow \vec{r} \cdot(3 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+6 \hat{k})=|-28| \end{aligned}$
Equation of $\pi_2$ in normal form is $\vec{r} \cdot \hat{n}_2=p_2$ i.e. $\vec{r} \cdot\left(\frac{3 \hat{i}+2 \hat{j}+6 \hat{k}}{7}\right)=\left|\frac{-28}{7}\right|=4 \Rightarrow p_2=4\Rightarrow p_1-p_2=7-4=3$ units.
